items.title: ACP image content blocks dropped before API call (persist_user_message override clobbers multimodal content)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

Image content blocks sent via the ACP adapter (`session/prompt` with an `image` content block) **never reach the model**. The model behaves as if no image was attached. This happens for **every** provider/model, independent of `promptCapabilities.image` and `_model_supports_vision` — the image is dropped *before* the request payload is built.

Reproduced on `v0.16.0` (upstream `3edd09a`).

## Root cause

`AIAgent._apply_persist_user_message_override` (`run_agent.py`) rewrites the current-turn user message in place:

```python
def _apply_persist_user_message_override(self, messages):
    idx = getattr(self, "_persist_user_message_idx", None)
    override = getattr(self, "_persist_user_message_override", None)
    if override is None or idx is None:
        return
    if 0 <= idx < len(messages):
        msg = messages[idx]
        if isinstance(msg, dict) and msg.get("role") == "user":
            msg["content"] = override   # <-- clobbers multimodal content
```

The ACP adapter passes a **text-only** `persist_user_message` for multimodal prompts (`acp_adapter/server.py`):

```python
result = agent.run_conversation(
    user_message=user_content,                         # list: [{type:text}, {type:image_url}]
    ...
    persist_user_message=user_text or "[Image attachment]",   # plain string
)
```

`build_turn_context` runs a **crash-resilience persist of the inbound user turn before the first API call**, which calls `_apply_persist_user_message_override(messages)` on the **same** `messages` list the conversation loop later reads to build `api_messages`. So the multimodal `content` list (`[{type:"text"}, {type:"image_url"}]`) is overwritten with the plain `persist_user_message` string **before** the request is assembled. The `image_url` part is gone end-to-end.

Because the strip happens this early, `_model_supports_vision()` / `_prepare_messages_for_non_vision_model()` are never even reached (the message no longer has image parts), and a fully vision-capable model still sees text only.

### Trace evidence

Instrumenting the ACP prompt handler and `_prepare_messages_for_non_vision_model`:

- At `acp_adapter/server.py` after `_content_blocks_to_openai_user_content(prompt)`: `user_content_shape=['text', 'image_url']` ✅
- At `_prepare_messages_for_non_vision_model` entry (just before the API call): user message `content` = `str(len=135)` ❌ — exactly the text-only `persist_user_message`, image dropped.

A direct provider call with the same `image_url` data URL (bypassing Hermes) works fine on a vision model, confirming the loss is internal to Hermes.

## Minimal repro

Drive `hermes acp` over stdio (line-delimited JSON-RPC): `initialize` → `session/new` → `session/prompt` with:

```json
{
  "sessionId": "<id>",
  "prompt": [
    { "type": "text", "text": "Reply with ONLY the dominant color word of the image. If you received no image, reply IMAGE_NOT_RECEIVED." },
    { "type": "image", "data": "<base64 of a solid-color PNG>", "mimeType": "image/png" }
  ]
}
```

With any vision-capable model configured (e.g. `openrouter/google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite`), the model replies `IMAGE_NOT_RECEIVED` instead of the color.

## Fix

Don't clobber multimodal list content — the synthetic-prefix cleanup the override exists for only applies to text turns:

```python
        if 0 <= idx < len(messages):
            msg = messages[idx]
            if isinstance(msg, dict) and msg.get("role") == "user":
                if isinstance(msg.get("content"), list):
                    return
                msg["content"] = override
```

With this, the same repro returns the correct color. Text-only turns are unaffected.

### Suggested cleaner fix

The override mutating the **shared** `messages` list (used for both the API call and persistence) is the underlying smell. A more robust fix would apply the clean/redacted `persist_user_message` only to a copy used for transcript/DB persistence, leaving the API-bound messages untouched — and for multimodal turns, persist a redacted form (e.g. text + `[image]` placeholder) so base64 blobs don't bloat the session DB while the image still reaches the model.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5), upstream `3edd09a`
- ACP adapter path (`hermes acp` over stdio)

## Bug Description

Korean IME (Microsoft 입력기) drops the final syllable when submitting via Enter in the Desktop composer. Typing "테스트" and pressing Enter sends "테스" instead.

Adding a trailing space ("테스트 ") or punctuation ("테스트.") resolves the issue — the IME flushes completely before submit.

## Root Cause

Windows Korean IME event sequence on Enter:

1. `keydown` (isComposing=true, keyCode=229) — fires BEFORE compositionend
2. `compositionend` — IME commits, flushEditorToDraft runs

The existing `isComposing` guard in `handleEditorKeyDown` works correctly for the 229 keydown. But on many Korean IME configurations, the 229 keydown is followed by a **second clean keydown** (isComposing=false) that fires **before** compositionend's flush propagates to React state. `submitDraft` then reads a stale draft value.

## Chinese IME (#39614) vs Korean IME

The existing fix for #39614 flushes DOM text in `onCompositionEnd`. This works for Chinese IME because `compositionend` fires after the DOM is fully populated with committed text. Korean IME has a different event sequence with keydown 229 firing mid-composition, which can trigger submit before the IME flushes.

## Test Sequence (Windows, Korean IME)

1. `안녕하세요` → last syllable `요` dropped
2. `설정 바꿔줘` → last syllable `줘` dropped
3. `테스트 ` (trailing space) → works correctly
4. `테스트.` (trailing period) → works correctly
5. `냉동기 가동시간 계산해줘` → `줘` dropped
6. Test with IME 호환 모드 toggle (Settings > Language > Korean > IME Options)

## Suggested Fix

**Part 1:** In `handleEditorKeyDown`, also check `event.keyCode === 229`:

```tsx
// line 679
if (composingRef.current || event.nativeEvent.isComposing || event.keyCode === 229) {
  return
}

Part 2: In submitDraft, read from live DOM instead of React state:

Code
· tsx
// Before:
const submitted = draft

// After:
const editorNode = editorRef.current
const submitted = editorNode ? composerPlainText(editorNode).trim() || draft : draft
Part 3: Add a test to ime-composition-dom-repro.test.tsx that simulates the Korean IME sequence:

compositionstart → textContent = "테스" → input → keyDown(229) → keyDown(clean) → compositionEnd → submit


## Environment

- Hermes Desktop (Electron)
- Windows 11, Korean IME (Microsoft 입력기)

# Bug Report: CLI Session Messages Not Persisted to SQLite DB

## Summary
When using `hermes chat` (CLI mode), pressing Ctrl+C at the idle prompt causes the session to exit without saving conversation messages to the SQLite session database. The session row is created but remains empty (0 messages in the `messages` table). The `ended_at` and `end_reason` fields are also left as NULL, indicating the cleanup path never runs.

## Environment
- **Hermes version**: hermes-agent (installed at ~/.hermes/hermes-agent)
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-124-generic
- **Model**: openrouter/owl-alpha
- **Provider**: openrouter
- **Python**: 3.12.3
- **Active profile**: default
- **Terminal backend**: local

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `hermes chat`
2. Have a conversation (send messages, get agent responses)
3. Press Ctrl+C at the idle prompt (agent not running)
4. Check session in SQLite: `~/.hermes/state.db`

## Expected Behavior
- All conversation messages should be persisted to the SQLite `messages` table
- The session's `ended_at` should be set to the exit timestamp
- The session's `end_reason` should be set to `cli_close`
- `hermes --resume <session_id>` should recover the full conversation

## Actual Behavior
- Session row exists in `sessions` table with `started_at` set
- `ended_at` is NULL (never closed)
- `end_reason` is NULL
- `message_count` in sessions table may show a non-zero value (updated by `end_session`) but the actual `messages` table has 0 rows for that session
- `hermes --resume <session_id>` shows 0 messages

## Evidence from SQLite DB

### Affected sessions (all CLI sessions today after ~10:06 AM)
| Session ID | Started | Ended | End Reason | DB message_count | Actual messages |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20260611_123219_3c116d | 12:32:29 | NULL | NULL | 83 | 0 |
| 20260611_111048_f436d3 | 11:10:48 | NULL | NULL | 0 | 0 |
| 20260611_111047_717770 | 11:10:47 | NULL | NULL | 0 | 0 |
| 20260611_100826_ccda49 | 10:08:26 | NULL | NULL | 0 | 0 |
| 20260611_100826_61f00b | 10:08:26 | NULL | NULL | 0 | 0 |
| 20260611_100826_a384d2 | 10:08:26 | NULL | NULL | 0 | 0 |
| 20260611_100643_11f21b | 10:06:43 | NULL | NULL | 0 | 0 |
| 20260611_100643_f74dcc | 10:06:43 | NULL | NULL | 0 | 0 |
| 20260611_100643_cef502 | 10:06:43 | NULL | NULL | 0 | 0 |

### Working sessions (for comparison)
| Session ID | Started | Ended | End Reason | Messages |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20260611_051008_0afd21 | 05:10:08 | 05:16:50 | resumed_other | 697 |
| 20260611_050833_52516d | 05:08:33 | 05:14:21 | cli_close | 646 |
| 20260610_115319_9a9f0f | Jun 10 11:53 | Jun 10 11:34 | compression | 801 |

### Key observations
1. 12 CLI sessions created today, 9 have NULL `ended_at` (never closed)
2. 9 sessions have 0 actual messages in the `messages` table
3. Sessions before ~10:06 AM today work correctly (messages persisted, proper end_reason)
4. The `message_count` column in the `sessions` table can be non-zero even when 0 messages exist (e.g., session 20260611_123219_3c116d shows message_count=83 but 0 rows in messages table) — this suggests `end_session()` updates the counter but `_flush_messages_to_session_db()` never wrote the actual messages

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue is in the CLI REPL's Ctrl+C handling and cleanup path:

1. `handle_ctrl_c()` (cli.py line 11323) handles Ctrl+C at the idle prompt
2. When the agent is NOT running and input buffer is empty, it sets `self._should_exit = True` and calls `event.app.exit()` (line 11417-11418)
3. The REPL's `run()` method should then execute cleanup code (lines 13060-13108) which calls:
   - `self._session_db.end_session(...)` to close the session
   - `_run_cleanup()` for resource cleanup
4. However, the cleanup code is NOT being reached — `ended_at` remains NULL for all affected sessions

The `_flush_messages_to_session_db()` is called during `_persist_session()` which runs:
- At the start of each turn (turn_context.py line 240) — "crash-resilience" persistence
- At the end of each turn (turn_finalizer.py line 143) — after agent finishes responding

If these paths are not executing (possibly due to an exception or early return), messages accumulate in memory but never get written to SQLite.

## Impact
- **Data loss**: All conversations from CLI sessions created after ~10:06 AM on 2026-06-11 are lost (cannot be recovered via `--resume`)
- **No recovery path**: The messages exist only in the terminal scrollback, not in any persistent storage
- **User experience**: Users who rely on `--resume` to continue conversations will find empty sessions

## Possible Fixes
1. Ensure the REPL cleanup path (cli.py lines 13060-13108) always runs on Ctrl+C, even if `event.app.exit()` raises an exception
2. Add a `try/finally` block around the REPL's `run()` method to guarantee cleanup
3. Add a signal handler for SIGINT that flushes messages before exiting
4. Consider writing messages to SQLite synchronously during each turn (not just at turn boundaries) to minimize data loss on abrupt exit

items.body:
### Bug Description

os.execvpe()` crashes the calling process with exit code `3221225477` (`STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` / `0xC0000005`) on Windows under Python 3.14.4. This was introduced by the dashboard multi-profile unification in PR #44007 (commit `875aa8f16`).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes Desktop on Windows with Python 3.14.4
2. Switch to a non-default profile (e.g. `creative`, `private`, `code`)
3. The profile backend process exits with code `3221225477`
4. The desktop log shows:
   ```
   [hermes] Hermes backend for profile "creative" exited (3221225477)
- **Every non-default profile** fails to launch its dashboard backend (creative, private, code, etc.)
- The crash loop spawns zombie dashboard processes on escalating port numbers (9121, 9122, 9123, ...), exhausting ports
- The default profile is **not** affected (it doesn't hit the re-exec code path)
- Intermittent: sometimes exits cleanly with code 0, other times crashes (depends on which native extension cleanup runs first)

### Expected Behavior

Being able to connect to other profiles. 

### Actual Behavior

goes to gateway offline on all profiles besides default.  In `hermes_cli/main.py`, `cmd_dashboard()` calls `os.execvpe()` to re-exec a named-profile dashboard process as the machine (default) dashboard:

```python
reexec_argv = [
    sys.executable, "-m", "hermes_cli.main",
    "-p", "default",
    "dashboard",
    "--port", str(args.port),
    "--host", args.host,
    "--open-profile", _launch_profile,
]
env = os.environ.copy()
env.pop("HERMES_HOME", None)
os.execvpe(sys.executable, reexec_argv, env)
```

On **Unix**, `os.execvpe()` atomically replaces the current process with the new one. On **Windows**, it calls `CreateProcess()` to spawn a child, then calls `Py_Exit(0)` to terminate the caller. The teardown via `Py_FinalizeEx()` causes a segfault in a native C extension during interpreter finalization, producing exit code `3221225477`.

**Confirmed by direct test:**
- Calling process exit code: `3221225477` (not `0`)
- No stdout/stderr output
- `atexit` handlers never execute
- Child process may or may not be created (race condition)


### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/fVumY
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/sBicx
  desktop.log  https://paste.rs/mDkjy
(failed to upload: agent.log: Failed to upload to any paste service:
  paste.rs: HTTP Error 500: Internal Server Error
  dpaste.com: <urlopen error [Errno 11004] getaddrinfo failed>)
```

### Operating System

Windows 10

### Python Version

3.14.4

### Hermes Version

v0.16.0 875aa8f16

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Replace the `os.execvpe()` re-exec on Windows with in-place dashboard startup (same as `--isolated`):

```python
if sys.platform == "win32":
    pass  # fall through to normal dashboard startup
else:
    # ... existing re-exec logic ...
    os.execvpe(sys.executable, reexec_argv, env)
```

This makes the dashboard run per-profile on Windows instead of unifying to a machine dashboard, but avoids the crash entirely and keeps Electron's process pool tracking intact.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

## Feature Request

### Problem
Hermes supports `custom_providers` in `config.yaml` for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, but these providers never appear in the model/provider selector UI — neither in the desktop app nor in the `hermes model` CLI picker. Users must manually set `model.provider: custom:<name>` in config.yaml via the terminal, which is invisible, not discoverable, and breaks the GUI-only workflow.

This affects anyone using custom endpoints: local inference (vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio), cloud proxies (Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock via custom bridge), API routers (AgentRouter, TokenRouter, OpenRouter alternatives), Codex/Command Code API, or any private deployment.

### Use Case
A user might have several custom endpoints configured:
- `custom:tokenrouter` (third-party API router with 97 models)
- `custom:vertex-gemini` (local Vertex AI proxy)
- `custom:command-code` (Command Code API)
- `custom:local-vllm` (self-hosted)

Currently, switching between these requires editing config.yaml — there is no way to select them from the GUI or CLI picker.

### Proposed Solution
1. **Desktop app:** In `model-picker.tsx` / `model-picker-overlay.tsx`, read the `custom_providers` config section and render each entry as a selectable provider option alongside built-in providers (OpenRouter, Anthropic, etc.).
2. **CLI (`hermes model`):** When the user selects the "custom" provider category, show the named entries from `custom_providers` as sub-options (e.g. `custom:tokenrouter`).
3. **Model discovery (nice-to-have):** Optionally call the custom provider's `/v1/models` endpoint to populate a model dropdown, with configurable timeout/cache.

- CLI picker tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_picker_*.py`
- Config section: `custom_providers` in `config.yaml`

### Why This Matters
Custom providers are the primary way Hermes integrates with self-hosted inference, private APIs, third-party routers, and emerging model APIs. As the ecosystem grows, the ability to switch between them through the normal UI (rather than editing config files) becomes essential for a smooth user experience — especially for desktop and gateway users who don't use the terminal.

items.title: Desktop terminal pane should follow agent backend (WSL/Docker/SSH)
items.body:
## Current behavior

The Hermes desktop app's embedded terminal pane (right sidebar, xterm.js + node-pty) always spawns PowerShell on Windows, regardless of the agent's configured terminal backend. When the agent runs in WSL2 (via `terminal.backend: "wsl"`), the embedded terminal remains in PowerShell, creating a disconnect:

- Agent commands execute in WSL via `wsl -e bash -c "..."`
- Terminal pane shows PowerShell, not the agent's WSL session
- `read_terminal` can't monitor what the agent is actually doing

## Desired behavior

The embedded terminal pane should auto-detect the agent's terminal backend and spawn the matching shell:

| Agent backend | Terminal pane shell |
|---|---|
| `local` | System default (PowerShell on Win, bash on Linux/macOS) |
| `wsl` | `wsl -e bash` (connected to the same WSL distro) |
| `docker` | `docker exec -it <container> bash` |
| `ssh` | SSH interactive session |

## Technical approach

Three changes needed:

### 1. React frontend (`use-terminal-session.ts`)
Pass the current backend to `terminalApi.start()`:

```ts
// Current
terminalApi.start({ cols: term.cols, cwd, rows: term.rows })

// Proposed
terminalApi.start({ cols: term.cols, cwd, rows: term.rows, backend })
```

Where `backend` is read from the app settings store (same value as `terminal.backend` in config.yaml).

### 2. Preload bridge (`preload.cjs`)
Forward the `backend` parameter:

```js
start: options => ipcRenderer.invoke('hermes:terminal:start', options),
```

### 3. Electron main process
In the `terminal:start` handler, switch the PTY spawn target based on `options.backend`:

```js
function getShellForBackend(backend, cwd) {
  switch (backend) {
    case 'wsl':
      return { file: 'wsl.exe', args: ['-e', 'bash', '-l'] };
    case 'docker':
      return { file: 'docker', args: ['exec', '-it', '-w', cwd, containerId, 'bash'] };
    default:
      return undefined; // use system default (node-pty auto-detects)
  }
}

const shell = getShellForBackend(options.backend, options.cwd);
pty.spawn(shell?.file || defaultShell, shell?.args || [], { cwd, cols, rows, ... });
```

## Scope

- Only affects the desktop app
- Backward compatible: if no `backend` is passed, behavior unchanged (system default shell)
- Stretch goal: terminal pane also displays the backend name in the title bar (e.g., "WSL: Debian" instead of "PowerShell")

## Related

- PR #44158 — WSL2 execution backend

```bash
hermes --profile auditor dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 19223
# → starts successfully (no HERMES_DESKTOP)
```

### Expected Behavior

1. Switching profiles in Hermes Desktop should work seamlessly — the backend for the selected profile starts without errors.

3. The desktop app should be usable regardless of which profile is set as the active/default.

1. Switching to a non-default profile in Hermes Desktop causes the pool backend to crash immediately with exit code `3221225477` (Windows) / `139` (Unix) — an `ACCESS_VIOLATION` / `SIGSEGV`.
2. The crash happens before the HTTP dashboard becomes ready — no "Waiting for Hermes backend to become ready" line ever appears.
3. If a non-default profile is set as the active profile via `hermes profile use`, the desktop becomes **completely unusable** on next boot — the primary backend crashes in the same way, creating an infinite crash loop.
4. The same profile works fine when launched via CLI **without** `HERMES_DESKTOP=1`.

### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
---

## Logs

### Desktop log (crash cycle)

[hermes] Starting Hermes backend for profile "auditor" via Hermes at ...hermes-agent (venv: ...hermes-agent\venv)
[hermes] Hermes backend for profile "auditor" exited (3221225477)

[hermes] Starting Hermes backend for profile "auditor" via Hermes at ...hermes-agent (venv: ...hermes-agent\venv)
[hermes] Hermes backend for profile "auditor" exited (3221225477)


**Note:** No "Waiting for Hermes backend to become ready" line appears between spawn and exit — crash happens during early startup, before the HTTP dashboard responds.

### Agent log (auditor profile — successful start before crashes began)

2026-06-11 20:32:44 INFO ... agent.conversation_loop: session started
2026-06-11 20:32:46 ... Session ran successfully: "Halo, ini auditor. Test koneksi."
2026-06-11 20:35:29 INFO hermes_cli.plugins: Plugin discovery complete: 38 found, 32 enabled


The profile **can** run successfully — the crash is intermittent and may be triggered by a specific state or timing.

### Event Viewer (Windows)

Faulting application: python.exe
Faulting module: unknown
Exception code: 0xc0000005 (ACCESS_VIOLATION)
```

### Operating System

Windows 11 Enterprise

### Python Version

3.11.15 (venv)

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · upstream a09343cc

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

## Root Cause Analysis

### Trigger chain

```
Electron main.cjs
  ├── startHermes()          # Primary backend — ✅ works
  │   env: { HERMES_DESKTOP='1', HERMES_HOME='<root>' }
  │   args: dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port>
  │         [+ optional --profile <name> via readActiveDesktopProfile()]
  │
  └── spawnPoolBackend()     # Non-default profile — 💥 crashes
      env: { HERMES_DESKTOP='1', HERMES_HOME='<profile_dir>' }
      args: --profile <name> dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port>
```

### Code locations

#### 1. Pool backend spawn (Electron)
**`apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs:4546-4564`** — `spawnPoolBackend()`:
```javascript
const child = spawn(backend.command, backend.args, {
  env: {
    ...process.env,
    HERMES_HOME,
    ...backend.env,
    HERMES_DESKTOP: '1',              // ← line 4559: crash trigger
    HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN: token,
    HERMES_WEB_DIST: webDist,
  },
  ...
});
```

#### 2. Primary backend spawn (Electron, same pattern)
**`apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs:4746-4765`** — `startHermes()`:
```javascript
hermesProcess = spawn(backend.command, backend.args, {
  env: {
    ...process.env,
    HERMES_HOME,
    ...backend.env,
    HERMES_DESKTOP: '1',              // ← same env var, but no crash here
    ...
  },
  ...
});
```

#### 3. Profile override (Python, import-time)
**`hermes_cli/main.py:336-422`** — `_apply_profile_override()`:
```python
os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = resolve_profile_env(profile_name)  # points to profiles/<name>/
```

#### 4. `HERMES_DESKTOP` consumers (Python)
| File | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| `tools/read_terminal_tool.py:51-53` | `check_fn` gates the `read_terminal` tool |
| `toolsets.py:36-38` | `read_terminal` in `_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS` |
| `hermes_cli/web_server.py:141` | Starts cron ticker daemon thread |
| `agent/prompt_builder.py:892` | Adds desktop hint to system prompt |

All of these are pure Python — none of them can cause a native segfault by themselves.

### Why it's a native crash

Exit code `0xC0000005` (Windows) / signal `SIGSEGV` (Unix) = **access violation**. This is **not** a Python `Exception` — it's a hardware fault from a **C extension module** (e.g. `tokenizers`, `faster-whisper`, `numpy`, or a browser automation native library).

The crash is triggered by the **combination** of:
1. `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` set in the child env
2. `HERMES_HOME` pointing to a **profile subdirectory** (`profiles/<name>/`) rather than the root hermes dir
3. One of the enabled tool plugins loading a native module that reads config/env from `HERMES_HOME` and crashes on an unexpected value or path

### Likely culprit

The `tools/read_terminal_tool.py` module's `check_fn` (`check_read_terminal_requirements`) returns `True` only when `HERMES_DESKTOP=1`. When the tool registry enumerates tools, this check triggers different import/code paths that may load native dependencies incompatible with the profile's config state.

---

### Proposed Fix (optional)



## Suggested Workaround / Fix

### Short-term (Electron patch in main.cjs)

In `spawnPoolBackend()`, either:

**Option A:** Remove `HERMES_DESKTOP` from the pool backend env (the `read_terminal` tool and cron ticker won't be available for non-default profile sessions):
```javascript
// Line 4557-4560 — omit HERMES_DESKTOP for pool backends
HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN: token,
// HERMES_DESKTOP: '1',  // ← remove this line
HERMES_WEB_DIST: webDist
```

**Option B:** Gate `HERMES_DESKTOP` behind a `check_fn` that verifies the profile can support it before setting it.

### Long-term (Hermes core)

Investigate which native C module crashes under `HERMES_HOME=<profile_dir>` + `HERMES_DESKTOP=1`. The fix is likely in one of:
- `python-dotenv` loading the profile's `.env` with `override=True`
- A browser/web/image-gen plugin's native dependency
- `faster-whisper` model initialization with profile-specific paths
---

## Fix Applied

### Analysis

PYTHONFAULTHANDLER trace captured the crash at **`os.execvpe()`** in `hermes_cli/main.py:10315`:

```
Windows fatal exception: access violation
Current thread 0x000063dc (most recent call first):
  File "<frozen os>", line 597 in _execvpe
  File "<frozen os>", line 583 in execvpe
  File "main.py", line 10315 in cmd_dashboard
```

The crash path:
1. Desktop spawns: `--profile auditor dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port X`
2. `cmd_dashboard()` in `main.py` detects non-default profile (`_launch_profile = "auditor"`)
3. Tries to **re-exec** as default profile: `os.execvpe(sys.executable, ['-p', 'default', 'dashboard', ...], env)`
4. On Windows, `os.execvpe` uses CRT's `_wexecvpe` → `CreateProcess`, which crashes with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` when the environment block contains unexpected state from `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` + profile env vars

### Fix in `hermes_cli/main.py`

**File:** `hermes_cli/main.py` (lines 10298-10315 → revised)
**Branch:** `cmd_dashboard` — profile consolidation logic

**Before:**
```python
reexec_argv = [sys.executable, "-m", "hermes_cli.main",
               "-p", "default", "dashboard", ...]
env = os.environ.copy()
env.pop("HERMES_HOME", None)
os.execvpe(sys.executable, reexec_argv, env)  # ← CRASH on Windows
```

**After:**
```python
if sys.platform != "win32":
    # POSIX: re-exec as default profile (true execve, same PID)
    reexec_argv = [sys.executable, "-m", "hermes_cli.main",
                   "-p", "default", "dashboard", ...]
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env.pop("HERMES_HOME", None)
    os.execvpe(sys.executable, reexec_argv, env)
# Windows: start dedicated dashboard in-place (--isolated semantics)
_launch_profile = ""
args.open_profile = ""
```

### Why this works

On Windows, `os.execvpe` does NOT replace the process (there's no `execve` syscall on Windows). The CRT emulates it by creating a new process and exiting the current one. This emulation can crash under specific env configurations. By contrast, running the dashboard in-place under the profile's `HERMES_HOME` is identical to `--isolated` mode, which is a fully supported and tested code path.

### Verification

| Test | Before fix | After fix |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` + `--profile auditor` dashboard start | 💥 Exit 139 (SIGSEGV) | ✅ Starts, responds on port |
| `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` + second instance same port | 💥 Same crash | ✅ "already running", exit 0 |
| Dashboard HTTP response | N/A | ✅ `{"detail":"Unauthorized"}` (correct — needs token) |

items.body:
## Summary

Since 5cd6c1717 (2026-05-23, #30719), `hermes gateway restart` refuses to run when `_HERMES_GATEWAY=1` is in the environment (hermes_cli/gateway.py, restart subcommand). The gateway sets that marker **process-wide** at import (`gateway/run.py:835` — `os.environ["_HERMES_GATEWAY"] = "1"`), and `_launch_detached_restart_command()` (gateway/run.py ~3981) spawns its successor helper via `subprocess.Popen` **without scrubbing the env**. The helper therefore inherits the marker, its `hermes gateway restart` exits 1 with "Refusing to restart the gateway from inside the gateway process", and the refusal is invisible (stdout/stderr → DEVNULL).

Net effect: on any platform where /restart takes the detached path — i.e. anywhere `INVOCATION_ID` (systemd) is unset and no container is detected — the in-chat `/restart` tears the gateway down, exits 0, and **nothing respawns it**.

## Observed live (macOS / launchd)

macOS 2026-06-08, launchd agent generated by an older Hermes (`KeepAlive {SuccessfulExit: false}`):

- `/restart` from Telegram → `gateway.exit_clean` in gateway-exit-diag.log → **no successor `gateway.start` ever appears** → gateway fully dark (no poller, no cron) until a manual `launchctl kickstart -k`.
- The helper's refusal never surfaces anywhere (DEVNULL).

Note: the #30719 defense exists to stop *agent-initiated* restart loops, but it also kills the gateway's **own** restart mechanism — the helper is guaranteed to run only after the old process has exited (its `while kill -0 $PID` wait loop), so it is not the in-process case the defense targets.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Scrub `_HERMES_GATEWAY` from the detached helper's child env** in `_launch_detached_restart_command()` (all three spawn branches: setsid/bash/Windows watcher). The helper runs strictly post-exit, so the anti-loop defense shouldn't apply to it.
2. Optionally: detect launchd as a service manager in the /restart handler (the comment there already says "systemd/launchd" but only `INVOCATION_ID` is checked). `XPC_SERVICE_NAME` is set by launchd (verified: `XPC_SERVICE_NAME=ai.hermes.gateway` in the agent's env) — routing macOS through the `via_service` path would use the exit-75 branch added in 5987b2431 and avoid the fragile detached helper entirely.

## Mitigation that works today

Current `generate_launchd_plist()` emits unconditional `KeepAlive: true`, which revives the clean exit — installs that refresh their plist (`hermes gateway install`) recover from /restart fine. But users who recover with raw `launchctl kickstart` never trigger plist regeneration, so older `SuccessfulExit:false` plists persist indefinitely — and the detached helper is silently dead code for everyone not under systemd/container either way.

## Environment

- Hermes `68a997fed` (also present at current HEAD by code inspection)
- macOS (darwin), Python 3.11.14, launchd LaunchAgent supervision

items.title: Gateway cached-agent reuse can leak _last_flushed_db_idx across turns and skip assistant transcript rows
items.body:
## Summary

When the gateway reuses a cached `AIAgent`, the per-agent SessionDB flush cursor can leak across turns.

`GatewayRunner._init_cached_agent_for_turn()` resets some per-turn state, but it does **not** realign `agent._last_flushed_db_idx` to the history actually passed into the new turn.

As a result, a reused agent can compute a `flush_from` offset that is too large for the current turn and silently skip persisting the assistant reply into `state.db`.

This leaves a transcript with multiple consecutive `user` rows and missing `assistant` rows, which then causes later turns to replay stale questions and produce "repeated" or blended answers.

This looks related to, but distinct from:

- #24187, where message repair shortens `messages` vs `conversation_history`
- #43849, which describes the user-visible symptom that a reply was delivered but no assistant row was persisted

## Observed Behavior

In a live gateway session, the user reported that each new reply kept dragging prior questions into the current answer.

Inspecting the session transcript showed a pattern like:

- assistant
- user
- user
- user
- user
- user
- user
- assistant

So the platform visibly delivered multiple assistant replies over time, but the durable SQLite transcript only retained the final one. On subsequent turns, Hermes loaded this broken history, triggered consecutive-user repair, and effectively merged several old user turns into the next prompt.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The critical pieces are:

1. `gateway/run.py` reuses cached agents:

   ```python
   if cached and cached[1] == _sig:
       agent = cached[0]
       self._init_cached_agent_for_turn(agent, _interrupt_depth)
   ```

2. `_init_cached_agent_for_turn()` currently resets only:

   - `_last_activity_ts`
   - `_last_activity_desc`
   - `_api_call_count`

   It does **not** reset or realign `_last_flushed_db_idx`.

3. `run_agent.py::_flush_messages_to_session_db()` later computes:

   ```python
   start_idx = len(conversation_history) if conversation_history else 0
   flush_from = max(start_idx, self._last_flushed_db_idx)
   for msg in messages[flush_from:]:
       ... append_message(...)
   ```

If the cached agent still carries `_last_flushed_db_idx` from the previous turn, the new turn can start flushing from a later index than the current `conversation_history` boundary. Then the assistant message for this turn is silently skipped.

## Why This Causes Repeated Answers

On the gateway success path, transcript writes assume the agent already persisted the DB rows:

```python
agent_persisted = self._session_db is not None
append_to_transcript(..., skip_db=agent_persisted)
```

So if the agent-side flush skips the assistant row, the gateway does not backfill it. The next inbound message then reloads a transcript containing several consecutive `user` rows with the assistant rows missing.

That broken replay state matches the repeated-answer symptom exactly:

- Hermes repairs/merges consecutive `user` messages
- old unanswered-looking questions get folded into the next prompt
- the new reply appears to repeat or drag in previous topics

## Minimal Regression Shape

A focused test should simulate:

1. Create a cached `AIAgent` for a gateway session
2. Run one turn so `_last_flushed_db_idx` becomes non-zero
3. Reuse the same cached agent for a second turn with freshly loaded `history`
4. Do **not** reset `_last_flushed_db_idx`
5. Persist the second turn
6. Assert that the second turn's assistant row is missing from SessionDB

Then apply the fix and assert the assistant row is present.

## Suggested Fix

When reusing a cached agent, realign the flush cursor to the history actually being replayed for this turn.

Two plausible fixes:

1. In the gateway path, after `agent_history` is built for the current turn, set:

   ```python
   agent._last_flushed_db_idx = len(agent_history)
   ```

2. Or more defensively, inside persistence, clamp / recompute `flush_from` so stale cached-agent state cannot skip the current turn.

The first option seems the most direct because `_last_flushed_db_idx` is turn-local persistence state, and cached-agent reuse is precisely where the stale value crosses turn boundaries.

## Expected Invariant

For every successful gateway turn:

> If a visible assistant response is produced, the session transcript for that turn must contain the corresponding assistant row.

## Environment

- Hermes gateway on macOS
- Profile-scoped gateway session
- Cached-agent reuse enabled in gateway
- SessionDB (`state.db`) is the canonical transcript store

## Summary

The voice-mode docs tell users to run:

```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
uv pip install -e ".[voice]"
```

On a fresh curl-installed Linux setup, this fails if the user has not activated the Hermes virtual environment first. The installer created `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv`, but the shell was still using system Python, so `uv pip install` reported that there was no virtual environment.

## Observed

After installing `uv` and running the documented command from `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`:

```
uv pip install -e ".[voice]"
```

`uv` refuses to run because no virtual environment is active.

In the install directory:

```
$ python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable); print(sys.prefix); print(sys.base_prefix)'
/usr/bin/python3
/usr
/usr

$ ./venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable); print(sys.prefix); print(sys.base_prefix)'
/home/ubuntu/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python
/home/ubuntu/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv
/home/ubuntu/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.11.15-linux-aarch64-gnu
```

## Workaround

Targeting the installer-created venv explicitly works:

```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
uv pip install --python ./venv/bin/python -e ".[voice]"
```

This installed `faster-whisper`, `sounddevice`, and `numpy` successfully.

## Suggested docs fix

Either document activation first:

```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
source venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[voice]"
```

or use the activation-independent form:

```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
uv pip install --python ./venv/bin/python -e ".[voice]"
```

The second form is more robust because it matches the curl installer layout directly and does not depend on the user's current shell state.

## Related but separate

After the Python packages were installed, importing `sounddevice` failed with `OSError: PortAudio library not found`. That appears covered by existing issue #18432; this issue is only about the docs command not targeting/activating the Hermes venv.

## Bug Description

`_sanitize_tool_pairs()` in `agent/context_compressor.py` (line 1618) properly fixes orphaned tool_call/tool_result pairs by:
1. Removing tool results whose call_id has no matching assistant tool_call
2. Inserting stub tool results for assistant tool_calls whose results were dropped

However, it is **only called after compression** (line 2151), not in the general pre-API-request sanitization pipeline in `agent/conversation_loop.py` (lines 579–646).

When message history gets corrupted during session save/load (e.g., after a long conversation with 130+ tool turns), the pre-request sanitization (`_repair_message_sequence`) fixes role alternation violations but does NOT fix tool_call/tool_result pairing. The API then rejects the request with:

This is **non-retryable** — the session is permanently wedged, requiring `/new`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a long conversation with 100+ tool calls (e.g., installing skills, reading/writing files)
2. Let the conversation end naturally
3. Start a new turn in the same session
4. If the message history was corrupted during save/load, the error appears

## Expected Behavior

`_sanitize_tool_pairs()` should run before every API request (or at minimum, when message role alternation violations are detected), not just after compression.

## Actual Behavior

The sanitizer only runs in the compression code path. If compression never fires (e.g., context below threshold), orphaned tool_calls go undetected and cause a permanent 400 error.

## Evidence

34 role alternation violations were detected and fixed, but the tool pairing was never checked.

## Proposed Fix

Move `_sanitize_tool_pairs()` call (or equivalent logic) from compression-only to the general pre-request sanitization in `conversation_loop.py`, likely right after `_repair_message_sequence()`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (commit 1c2189839)
- DeepSeek v4 Pro provider
- Linux (Ubuntu)
- Compression config: threshold=0.15, target_ratio=0.12 (NOT triggered — session was at ~100K tokens, well below threshold)

```python
    "sounddevice==0.5.5",
    "numpy==2.4.3",
),
```

`faster-whisper` requires `av>=11` transitively. When transitive resolution fails (corrupted venv, interrupted install), `av` is missing and `import faster_whisper` raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'av'`.

### Reproduction

1. Configure `stt.enabled=true` + `stt.provider=local`
2. Ensure `av` is not installed
3. Trigger STT - raises ModuleNotFoundError

### Evidence

```
python -c "import faster_whisper" => ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'av'
pip check => faster-whisper 1.2.1 requires av, which is not installed.
```

### Suggested Fix

Add `av` explicitly: `"av>=11"`

items.body:
### Problem

`tools/lazy_deps.py:538-552` - active_features() uses _is_present() which checks only if a package name exists at any version.

If aiohttp 3.14.1 is installed by any dependency, platform.slack is reported as active because its spec aiohttp==3.13.4 matches on package name. Then refresh_active_features() triggers pip install aiohttp==3.13.4 - a downgrade.

### Impact

- Unnecessary pip operations during hermes update
- Potential downgrade from working to older pinned version
- On Windows, downgrade can fail if gateway holds .pyd files open

### Suggested Fix

Option A: Use _is_satisfied() instead of _is_present() in active_features().
Option B: Only match on the feature's primary package (first spec).

### Problem or Use Case

The global `-p` / `--profile` flag works for some gateway commands (`hermes -p stock gateway status`) but `hermes -p stock gateway start` fails with "service not installed" unless the profile has been separately registered as a systemd service. 

The only way to run the gateway under a non-default profile today is:
1. Change the active default profile: `hermes profile use stock`
2. Restart the gateway: `hermes gateway restart`

This is inconvenient when a user wants different profiles for different use cases (e.g., stock research on WeChat vs coding via CLI), because changing the default profile affects all future CLI sessions too.

Also, restarting the gateway while keeping a running profile (e.g., the WeChat gateway on `stock`) should be possible without switching the user's default profile for CLI sessions.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `--profile <name>` argument to the `hermes gateway` subcommand group:

```bash
hermes gateway start --profile stock
hermes gateway restart --profile dev
hermes gateway status --profile stock
```

When `--profile` is supplied, the gateway process should:
1. Set `HERMES_HOME` to `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/` at startup
2. Load config, .env, skills, and memory from that profile
3. Register as a separate service instance (if using systemd) so multiple gateway instances can coexist

The implementation can reuse the existing `_apply_profile_override()` mechanism in `hermes_cli/main.py` which already resolves `--profile` and sets `HERMES_HOME` before module imports — the main work would be threading it through to the gateway subcommand parser.

For systemd users, each profile's gateway should get a distinct service name (e.g., `hermes-gateway@stock`, `hermes-gateway@dev`) to allow independent lifecycle management.

### Alternatives Considered

1. **Use the global `-p` flag**: Already exists but incomplete — `hermes -p stock gateway start` fails with "service not installed" and there's no clean way to manage per-profile gateway lifecycle.

2. **Manually switch default profile**: `hermes profile use stock && hermes gateway restart` works but is disruptive — it changes the default for ALL future CLI sessions, not just the gateway.

3. **Run separate Hermes installations**: Install Hermes in different locations for each profile. Works but is heavy, duplicates the entire codebase, and loses the unified state management that profiles provide.

4. **Use wrapper scripts**: Create shell aliases that set HERMES_HOME before calling gateway commands. Fragile and doesn't integrate with the service management system.

The proposed `--profile` flag is the most native, discoverable, and maintainable solution that builds on Hermes' existing profile infrastructure.

items.title: feat: Show custom_providers in model/provider selector (desktop + CLI)
items.body:
## Feature Request

### Problem
Hermes supports `custom_providers` in `config.yaml` for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, but these providers never appear in the model/provider selector UI — neither in the desktop app nor in the `hermes model` CLI picker. Users must manually set `model.provider: custom:<name>` in config.yaml via the terminal, which is invisible, not discoverable, and breaks the GUI-only workflow.

This affects anyone using custom endpoints: local inference (vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio), cloud proxies (Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock via custom bridge), API routers (AgentRouter, TokenRouter, OpenRouter alternatives), Codex/Command Code API, or any private deployment.

### Use Case
A user might have several custom endpoints configured:
- `custom:tokenrouter` (third-party API router with 97 models)
- `custom:vertex-gemini` (local Vertex AI proxy)
- `custom:command-code` (Command Code API)
- `custom:local-vllm` (self-hosted)

Currently, switching between these requires editing config.yaml — there is no way to select them from the GUI or CLI picker.

### Proposed Solution
1. **Desktop app:** In `model-picker.tsx` / `model-picker-overlay.tsx`, read the `custom_providers` config section and render each entry as a selectable provider option alongside built-in providers (OpenRouter, Anthropic, etc.).
2. **CLI (`hermes model`):** When the user selects the "custom" provider category, show the named entries from `custom_providers` as sub-options (e.g. `custom:tokenrouter`).
3. **Model discovery (nice-to-have):** Optionally call the custom provider's `/v1/models` endpoint to populate a model dropdown, with configurable timeout/cache.

### Relevant Code
- Desktop picker: `apps/desktop/src/components/model-picker.tsx`
- Desktop overlay: `apps/desktop/src/app/model-picker-overlay.tsx`
- CLI picker tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_picker_*.py`
- Config section: `custom_providers` in `config.yaml`

### Why This Matters
Custom providers are the primary way Hermes integrates with self-hosted inference, private APIs, third-party routers, and emerging model APIs. As the ecosystem grows, the ability to switch between them through the normal UI (rather than editing config files) becomes essential for a smooth user experience — especially for desktop and gateway users who don't use the terminal.

items.title: Codex gpt-5.5 autoraise should defer to external context engines

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

When an external context engine is active (`context.engine: lcm`), the Codex gpt-5.5 compression autoraise still overrides the host compression threshold to 85% and emits the Codex notice:

```text
ℹ Codex gpt-5.5 caps context at 272K, so auto-compaction was raised to 85% (from 50%) to use more of the window before summarizing.
  Opt back out: hermes config set compression.codex_gpt55_autoraise false
```

That is sensible for the built-in `ContextCompressor` at the stock 50% threshold, but it conflicts with external context engines such as `hermes-lcm`, where the plugin owns compaction policy and may already be using a benchmark-backed preset.

## Concrete case

Local operator setup:

```yaml
context:
  engine: lcm

compression:
  enabled: true
  threshold: 0.75
```

`hermes-lcm` active preset/config:

```bash
LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD=0.75
LCM_FRESH_TAIL_COUNT=24
LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS=8000
```

`lcm_status` reports the GPT/Codex long-context preset suggestion and keeps `context_threshold: 0.75`.

But Hermes core still applies the Codex gpt-5.5 route override unless the user explicitly sets:

```yaml
compression:
  codex_gpt55_autoraise: false
```

## Why this is a bug

The autoraise logic is host-side and model-route-specific:

- `agent/auxiliary_client.py::_compression_threshold_for_model(...)`
- `agent/agent_init.py` reads `compression.codex_gpt55_autoraise`, defaults it to `True`, and raises the threshold to `0.85` for `openai-codex + gpt-5.5`

That makes sense when the built-in compressor owns the threshold. It is surprising when `context.engine` is an external plugin.

For LCM, the 75% threshold is not “wasting the window”; it is the plugin’s chosen operating point. Raising it to 85% is a competing policy decision.

## Expected behavior

When `context.engine` is not the built-in/default compressor, Hermes should not silently apply the Codex gpt-5.5 `0.85` threshold override over the external engine’s policy.

Possible acceptable fixes:

1. Disable `compression.codex_gpt55_autoraise` automatically when `context.engine != "compressor"`.
2. Suppress the notice and leave threshold ownership to the active context engine.
3. Let context engines expose a capability such as `owns_threshold_policy = True` or `suppress_host_model_threshold_overrides = True`.
4. At minimum, document that LCM-style external engines should set:

```yaml
compression:
  threshold: 0.75
  codex_gpt55_autoraise: false
```

## Acceptance criteria

- With `context.engine: lcm`, `openai-codex + gpt-5.5` does not auto-raise the active compaction threshold from the engine/preset policy to 85%.
- The Codex gpt-5.5 notice is not shown when no host-side threshold change actually applies.
- Built-in compressor behavior is preserved: stock Hermes can still auto-raise 50% → 85% for Codex gpt-5.5.
- The fix composes with existing preflight/status work.

## Related issues

- #25115 — broader request for alternative context engines to suppress/customize generic preflight compression status.
- #42187 — related notice-repeat issue for the same Codex gpt-5.5 autoraise message.

## Workaround

Set this explicitly:

```bash
hermes config set compression.threshold 0.75
hermes config set compression.codex_gpt55_autoraise false
```

Then restart the gateway/session so the config is reloaded.

items.title: Add a Hermes-native child session terminal continuation seam
items.body:
## Goal
Provide a Hermes-native way for gateway/plugin code to register a callback or continuation that fires when a child session reaches a terminal state.

## Motivation
Gateway plugins can currently start child sessions via `gateway.start_child_session(...)`, but there does not appear to be a minimal, explicit seam for "tell me when this session finishes". Consumers such as Hermes Issue Runner should not have to poll GitHub labels, session DB rows, logs, or process state just to know whether a child session reached a terminal state.

## Desired shape
A minimal API that lets a caller:

1. Start or identify a child session (`session_id` / `session_key`).
2. Register interest in that session reaching a terminal state.
3. Receive a terminal result such as `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, or provider/quota failure.

This can be an event, callback, future/awaitable, webhook-style dispatch, or another Hermes-native primitive. The important constraint is that consumers should not implement their own polling loops.

## Non-goals for first pass
- Do not design a full workflow engine.
- Do not require issue-runner-specific GitHub knowledge in Hermes core.
- Durability across gateway restart is desirable, but this issue is intentionally a minimal placeholder for refining the right Hermes-native abstraction later.

## Related context
This came out of `zero-two-rafaeltab/hermes-issue-runner` issue #26, where the issue runner should stop polling GitHub labels to determine whether a child implementation session has finished.

items.title: [Bug]: Archive path still 400s after #44138 — PATCH endpoint allowlist missing 'archived' field
items.body:
## Summary

PR #44138 closes the *delete* half of #44117 but does not close the *archive* half. The desktop's `setSessionArchived()` is changed to send `{ archived: true, profile: 'elizabeth-engineer' }`, but the server's PATCH endpoint still rejects the body with HTTP 400 "Unsupported session fields: archived, profile". This trades a 404 (routing) for a 400 (validation) — same user-visible bug, smaller surface.

## Verification

I checked out the PR branches locally and confirmed the gap:

```
$ for ref in main pr-44138 pr-44162 pr-41772; do
    git show $ref:gateway/platforms/api_server.py | sed -n '1440,1450p'
  done
```

`api_server.py` PATCH handler is **byte-identical** across `main`, `pr-44138`, `pr-44162`, and `pr-41772`:

```python
allowed = {"title", "end_reason"}
unknown = sorted(set(body) - allowed)
if unknown:
    return web.json_response(_openai_error(
        f"Unsupported session fields: {', '.join(unknown)}",
        code="unsupported_session_field"), status=400)
```

`grep archived gateway/platforms/api_server.py` returns **zero hits** in every one of those four branches. The endpoint has no path that calls `db.set_session_archived()` and no path that uses the PATCH body's `profile` value to open the owning profile's `state.db`.

Meanwhile, in `pr-44138`'s `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts`:

```typescript
export function setSessionArchived(id, archived, profile?) {
  return window.hermesDesktop.api({
    ...(profile ? { profile } : {}),
    path: `/api/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`,
    method: 'PATCH',
    body: { archived, ...(profile ? { profile } : {}) }
  })
}
```

So the desktop will send `{ archived: true, profile: 'elizabeth-engineer' }` → server validates → `unknown = ['archived', 'profile']` → **HTTP 400**.

The PR description claims the endpoint "already reads `body.profile`" via a "SessionRename model". That model does not exist at the PATCH handler — it is a flat allowlist with no `SessionRename` indirection. The PR's backend tests cover DELETE with `?profile=` (which works) but do **not** cover the PATCH archive path, so the gap slips through review.

## Reproduction

1. macOS 26.3, Hermes Desktop packaged app (v0.16.0 / main @ `93a2f680f`).
2. Two profiles: `default` (primary) and `elizabeth-engineer` (pool/secondary).
3. elizabeth-engineer has 22 sessions / 6,309 messages in its `state.db`.
4. Open the desktop sidebar — elizabeth sessions are listed (read path works).
5. Right-click any of them → Archive → **HTTP 400 "Unsupported session fields: archived, profile"** (post-#44138), instead of the previous 404 "Session not found" (pre-#44138).

The 400 is just as user-visible a failure as the 404. The session is not archived, the sidebar row stays.

## Proposed fix

Extend the PATCH handler at `gateway/platforms/api_server.py:1432-1458`:

1. Add `"archived"` and `"profile"` to the `allowed` set.
2. If `body.get("profile")` is set, resolve the session ID against that profile's `state.db` (parity with how `deleteSession`'s `?profile=` is supposed to be handled in the same PR).
3. If `"archived" in body`, call `db.set_session_archived(session_id, bool(body["archived"]))`.
4. Add a backend test asserting:
   - `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` with `body={"archived": true, "profile": "elizabeth-engineer"}` returns 200 and the row's `archived` column flips to 1
   - The same call without `profile` still 400s (or 404s, depending on intended behavior), so we don't accidentally widen the API
   - The same call against the default profile's session without `profile` still works (no regression on the single-profile case)

The PR also needs the equivalent fix in the web dashboard (`hermes_cli/web_server.py`'s PATCH handler) if the web dashboard has an archive action — `pr-44162` only fixed the *read* path, not the write path.

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS 26.3
- **Hermes version:** v0.16.0 (June 5) and main @ `93a2f680f` (June 11) — both ship with the bug
- **Profile layout:** default (primary) + elizabeth-engineer (pool/secondary, 22 sessions)
- **Workaround until this lands:** `SessionDB.set_session_archived(sid, True)` from Python (bypasses both the routing and the PATCH allowlist)

## Related

- #44117 — original report ("Cannot delete sessions in default profile / ID not found")
- #44138 — partial fix (delete only)
- #44147 — web dashboard read-path cousin (separate fix in #44162)
- #44162 — web dashboard message read fix
- #41772 — gateway-restart recovery (different code path, same symptom)

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop /compress returns "not a quick/plugin/skill command: compress" — TUI command.dispatch doesn't redirect built-ins to slash.exec

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

## Bug Description

In Hermes Desktop, typing the built-in slash command `/compress` returns an error and does nothing:

    /compress - error: not a quick/plugin/skill command: compress

The conversation is **not** compressed; the error is returned before any compression code runs. The same `/compress` works correctly in the classic CLI (`hermes` command), so this is a routing bug specific to the Desktop → TUI gateway bridge.

Other built-in slash commands (e.g. `/model`, `/goal`, `/personality`, `/status`, `/config`, `/history`, `/save`, `/title`, `/reload`, `/stop`, `/fast`, `/debug`) likely have the same problem but were not individually verified.

This problem does not exist in the CLI version of my Hermes setup

## Related Issues

This is the same routing-class bug as:

- **#37254** — `[Bug]: TUI gateway command.dispatch doesn't handle skill bundles — deadlocks on /bundle-name` (open, P2). The reporter noted that fixing `command.dispatch` alone is insufficient; `slash.exec` also needs a redirect. A 3-patch fix pattern is documented there.
- **#43053** — `[Bug]: Quick calling of skills not working` (closed). Same exact error string but for skill commands. Fixed by PR #43120, which only improved error reporting — does not address built-in commands.
- **#12130** — TUI v2 feature-parity audit. Documents the architectural split: v1 CLI has 48 `CommandDef` entries; v2 TUI registers only ~25 locally and relies on a fall-through to `slash.exec`/`command.dispatch` for the rest. The fall-through is buggy.


### Steps to Reproduce

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Hermes Desktop (Electron app)
2. Type `/compress` in the chat composer and press Enter
3. Wait ~1 minute
4. Observe the error message; the conversation context is unchanged

### Expected Behavior


## Expected vs Actual Behavior

- **Expected:** `/compress` runs the compression logic and reports a result (e.g. `🗜️ Compressed: N → M messages`).


### Actual Behavior

- **Actual:** Error returned, no compression, context length unchanged.

### Affected Component

Other, Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Debug report uploaded:
  Report       https://paste.rs/3CVz1
  agent.log    https://paste.rs/eh3vG
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/9pBWy
  desktop.log  https://paste.rs/Ce18q
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 22.04

### Python Version

3.10.12

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · upstream c3464ecf Project: /home/maher/.hermes/hermes-agent Python: 3.11.15 OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0 Up to date

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

## Root Cause

The Desktop → TUI gateway bridge has **two** slash-command dispatch methods in `tui_gateway/server.py`:

| Method              | Line   | What it knows about                                                                                              |
| ------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `slash.exec`        | ~8618  | All built-in commands (`/compress`, `/model`, `/goal`, `/personality`, etc.) — handler at line 8596              |
| `command.dispatch`  | ~7562  | Only quicks, plugins, and skills — returns the generic error at line 7884 if none match                        |

For some reason, the Desktop routes `/compress` to `command.dispatch` instead of `slash.exec`. There is no built-in-command fallthrough in `command.dispatch`.

### Error site — `tui_gateway/server.py:7884`

```python
return _err(rid, 4018, f"not a quick/plugin/skill command: {name}")
```

### Working handler that should be reached — `tui_gateway/server.py:8596`

```python
elif name == "compress" and agent:
    _compress_session_history(session, arg)
    _sync_session_key_after_compress(sid, session)
    _emit("session.info", sid, _session_info(agent, session))
```

The `compress` handler in `_mirror_slash_side_effects` is correctly implemented and is also listed in the `_MUTATES_WHILE_RUNNING` set at line 8580, so the logic exists — it's purely a routing failure.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

## Suggested Fix Direction

Apply the same 3-patch pattern as #37254:

1. **`command.dispatch` (~line 7562):** Before the quick/plugin/skill lookups, add a built-in command check. If `name` is a known built-in, return a structured redirect to `slash.exec` (e.g. `f"built-in command: use slash.exec for /{name}"`) — or handle it directly.
2. **`slash.exec` (~line 8618):** Add a symmetric guard ensuring built-ins reach the existing handlers (line 8596 for `compress`, etc.).
3. **Tab completion (`commands.catalog` / `complete.slash`):** Verify built-ins are still listed and that typing them doesn't send the request to `command.dispatch` instead of `slash.exec`.

A definitive list of affected built-ins can be derived from `hermes_cli/commands.py::CommandDef` minus the v2 local registry in `ui-tui/src/app/slash/`.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop (Electron) — `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/linux-unpacked/Hermes`
- OS: Linux
- CLI (`hermes` command) works correctly with the same install
- TUI gateway file: `tui_gateway/server.py`
- Relevant lines: 7562, 7884, 8580, 8596, 8618

## Bug Description

Dashboard "Managed Files" (file browser) returns **HTTP 500** when accessed remotely on a **non-Docker** host. The error is:

```
Error: 500: {"detail":"Managed files root is unavailable: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/opt/data'"}
```

This affects any non-localhost access (Tailscale IP, LAN, reverse proxy, etc.) on bare-metal or desktop installations where `/opt/data` does not exist.

## Root Cause

In `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, `_managed_files_policy()` (line ~1038) combines two unrelated conditions with `OR`:

```python
if not _local_dashboard_request(request) or _default_hermes_root_is_opt_data():
    root = _ensure_managed_root(_HOSTED_MANAGED_FILES_ROOT)  # /opt/data
```

- `not _local_dashboard_request(request)` — `True` when the client IP is not `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`/`::1` (e.g., accessed via Tailscale `100.x.x.x`)
- `_default_hermes_root_is_opt_data()` — `True` inside Docker containers where `HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`

Because these are `OR`-ed, **any** non-localhost request forces the root to `/opt/data` — even on macOS/Linux hosts where that path doesn't exist and `/opt` is root-owned.

The constant `_HOSTED_MANAGED_FILES_ROOT = Path("/opt/data")` (line 913) is only valid inside the Docker container.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes on macOS or Linux (not Docker)
2. Run the dashboard with `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --insecure`
3. Access the dashboard from a non-localhost address (e.g., Tailscale IP like `100.x.x.x:9119`)
4. Navigate to the Files page

## Expected Behavior

The file browser should open, rooted at `~/.hermes` (or `HERMES_HOME`), allowing file management.

## Actual Behavior

HTTP 500 with `"Managed files root is unavailable: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/opt/data'"`

The `_ensure_managed_root()` function tries `Path("/opt/data").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` which fails because `/opt` is owned by root on standard macOS/Linux installs.

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS (also affects Linux bare-metal installs)
- **Hermes:** local install (not Docker)
- **Access method:** Remote (Tailscale IP, not localhost)
- **Hermes home:** `~/.hermes` (not `/opt/data`)

## Suggested Fix

Split the combined condition so that `/opt/data` is only used when actually running in Docker:

```python
# Docker: always use /opt/data
if _default_hermes_root_is_opt_data():
    root = _ensure_managed_root(_HOSTED_MANAGED_FILES_ROOT) if create_root else _HOSTED_MANAGED_FILES_ROOT
    return ManagedFilesPolicy(default_path=root, locked_root=root, can_change_path=False)

# Remote non-Docker: lock to HERMES_HOME (not /opt/data)
if not _local_dashboard_request(request):
    remote_root = get_hermes_home()
    root = _ensure_managed_root(remote_root) if create_root else remote_root
    return ManagedFilesPolicy(default_path=root, locked_root=root, can_change_path=False)
```

This preserves the Docker behavior, fixes non-Docker remote access (locked to `HERMES_HOME`), and leaves local access unchanged (home directory, unrestricted browsing).

## Workaround

Set the `HERMES_DASHBOARD_FILES_ROOT` environment variable before starting the dashboard:

```bash
export HERMES_DASHBOARD_FILES_ROOT=~/.hermes
hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --insecure
```

items.body:
### Summary

Add a generic **`command`** secret source: resolve credentials at startup by running a user-configured helper that prints the secret(s) on stdout, instead of keeping keys in plaintext `~/.hermes/.env`.

This is the lowest-common-denominator backend for the `agent/secret_sources/` framework (the same one `bitwarden.py` lives in): any secret store with a CLI works through it without a bespoke integration — `keepassxc-cli`, `secret-tool`, `pass`, `gpg`, or a script that `cat`s a tmpfs env file.

### Motivation

`.env` is currently the only place provider keys can live. Users who keep secrets in a local vault have no way to feed them to the agent without copying them back out to plaintext. The existing Bitwarden source covers a cloud secret manager; a generic command/exec source covers everything else — especially fully-offline / local-vault setups — with a single small, well-tested code path rather than one integration per vendor.

It complements (does not duplicate) the vendor-specific source requests already filed under the secrets roadmap:
- #3630 — feat(secrets): Phase 4 — Advanced Security (External Vaults) [parent epic]
- #22791 — Infisical backend
- #36949 — 1Password (`op://`) backend
- #30649 — Proton Pass backend
- #33126 — native Vaultwarden support

A generic command source is the substrate several of those could shell out to, and it ships parity with the Hermes desktop app's existing `command` secrets provider.

### Proposed design

- New `agent/secret_sources/command.py` mirroring the desktop TypeScript provider's security model: the requested key travels only in `HERMES_SECRET_KEY` (never interpolated into the `/bin/sh -c` string); hard timeout + output cap; cross-key misroute guard; base64-padding disambiguation; structured-only logging (never the command string or secret values); reuses `FetchResult`.
- A unified `secrets.provider` selector (`env` | `command` | `bitwarden`) so there's one source-of-truth for the active backend. `env` stays the default; a bare `secrets.bitwarden.enabled: true` is treated as `provider: bitwarden` for backward compatibility.
- POSIX-only (needs `/bin/sh`); on Windows it degrades to the `env` provider with a warning.
- Config (selector, command path, timeouts) lives in `config.yaml` under `secrets:`; only resolved secret values touch env.

### Scope

This issue tracks the agent-side `command` source + unified selector only. Desktop already has the counterpart provider; a follow-up will add the cross-surface onboarding/manager UI and CLI parity (`hermes secrets setup/status/test`).
